cells.tense: You are here with the pen, tending what grows, and you can see it take.
cells.ask: Show one person what you have grown and how it turned out, plainly, without explaining your method.
cells.core:
You are in the room where the work happens, and you can feel how much is going right. Things you have cared for are coming through — enough that you can stop steering and let the outcome happen.

The way back now is completion. You get to let go when the work is done, and let that be the good part. So show someone the thing you've grown. Not the process, not a defense, just what's there now. It will be more legible to them than you expect, and that is what lets this balance keep feeding the next thing instead of guarding this one.
cells.sheetLine: What you grew is here, let it stand.
cells.verb: tending what is growing until it stands on its own
cells.place: the work bench where you care for what is growing

cells.tense: You are already living in a harvest that hasn't arrived, and your hands are moving ahead of it.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you're growing and leave it alone until it can be handled without your hand in it.
cells.core:
There is a future version of this where the harvest is in and the people around you finally understand what you were growing. You are standing there now, and it makes you push the thing in front of you harder than it can take.

The pressure has become the care. You count the buds, water them again, check whether the outcome is ready to be seen. Care that clutches stops being care. There is a you that can dream from what's actually here instead of what hasn't come in yet — a vision that has already digested the real. Let one thing grow without your hand on it for a while. It will still be there when you look.
cells.sheetLine: You are forcing next season's harvest into this one.

cells.tense: You are still standing at the gate of a garden you walked out of, asking whether it's okay to tend again.
cells.ask: Choose one thing growing near you and give it ten minutes of attention today — no outcome required.
cells.core:
The caring stopped, not the ability. Something back there told you that tending would drain you or wouldn't be wanted, and you have been standing at that door since, deciding it's still real.

What is empty is the direction, not the soil. You don't get out of this by caring harder where you are now. You get out by picking one thing that is actually growing and giving it your time. That could be a plant, a person's project, your own health. Ten minutes of attention, no promise attached. The ability to see where it's going comes back from that, not before.
cells.sheetLine: The caring stopped, not the ability to care.

cells.tense: You are already tending a room you have not put your name on.
cells.ask: Tell someone what you are growing and that you meant to grow it.
cells.core:
You are already doing the caring. Things around you are growing because of attention you have been giving quietly, and you file it under 'it just happened' or 'that's what you do.' The care is running. Your name isn't on it.

When you only count what is finished, the work itself stays invisible — even to you. This is simpler, not harder. Say what you are growing, and say that you meant to. Not a report on the method. Just what is alive because of you, owned out loud. That is the release that lets you recognize what you were up to, and it is the same act that lets the work reach completion instead of dropping off the edge of your account.
cells.sheetLine: You are growing it, say it is yours.

The sentence that serves me, not them: 'You are the one deciding what gets passed on, and you know it.' — that is an admiring claim, and I am cutting it.
